name: sellers
title: Sellers
summary: Seller admission and the seller account: the Sell with us programme and multi-step application, verification checks and review decisions, seller statuses with account status, product approval and payout readiness kept separate, setup and launch readiness, storefront profile and public storefront, seller members and permissions, performance against targets, warnings, restrictions, suspensions and appeals.
owns: Sell with us programme information: requirements, eligible categories, example fees, payout timing, service targets and agreement versions
Seller application draft with six steps (account, business, verification, payout, return address, agreement), documents and versioned agreement acceptance
Verification checks (identity, business registration, tax id, payout account match, return address) and Trust and Risk referral
Application review: assign, request information with a deadline, approve (optionally with conditions), reject with an explanation, reapply date and appeal
Seller account status: Applied, Information required, Under review, Approved, Restricted, Suspended, Closed
Verified seller label: what was checked, what was not, when it lapses
Setup checklist after approval and the launch readiness review
Storefront profile (name, logo, banner, introduction, location, contact options, warranty text, featured collections) and staff review of store name changes, public claims and brand affiliation
Seller members, invitations, role templates and seller permissions (owner-only staff management and payout destination changes)
Payout destination entry by the owner (tokenised with the payout provider) and its readiness mirror
Business details and change requests for legal name and ownership
Performance metrics against targets (dispatch reliability, cancellations, valid tracking, returns, response time, unresolved cases, policy violations), warnings
Restrictions (reason, affected activity, scope, what still works, how to resolve, appeal route, review date), suspensions with a second reviewer, reinstatement, closure
Appeals against restrictions, suspensions and application rejections, decided by someone other than the original decider
notOwns: Sign-in, member accounts, invitation links and seller context switching: identity (sellers writes seller access through grantSellerContext / revokeSessions)
Payout destination verification (micro-deposits, re-authentication, review), balances, holds and payouts: finance
Return terms and the seller's return address after approval: returns (the application's return address is handed over on approval)
Shipping coverage and rates: shipping. Product review: catalog. Offer eligibility: offers (reacts to restriction events)
Seller support requests (seller/help, CS- references, SLAs): support
Seller feedback ratings: reviews. Notification preferences per member: notifications
Agreement texts and their versions: content policies (sellers stores which version was accepted)

stateMachines.name: Seller account status
stateMachines.notes: The plan's seven statuses. A seller row is created on submit (applied). Rejection, withdrawal and expiry close the row with closedReason; reopenOnAppeal applies only when closedReason = application_rejected and an appeal is overturned. Restricted = at least one active restriction; adding more keeps it restricted. Suspend takes effect only after the second reviewer approves (access approval request); until then the suspension row is pending_approval and the status does not change. Suspending or restricting never blocks existing orders, returns, cases, messages or (unless finance holds them) payouts (scenario 7). Account status, product approval (catalog) and payout readiness (finance) are separate fields everywhere.

stateMachines.name: Seller application
stateMachines.notes: Submit is blocked (APPLICATION_INCOMPLETE, details.missing) until every step is complete and all current agreement versions are accepted. Approve is blocked (CHECKS_UNRESOLVED) while a check is failed or needs attention without an accepted note. Reject requires reasonCode, an explanation the applicant reads and a reapply rule. Approval does not publish products or enable payouts.

stateMachines.name: Restriction
stateMachines.notes: Created directly as active when the caller's limit allows it (access); otherwise pending_approval until a second reviewer decides. Editing an active restriction (scope, reason, review date) is audited and republished as sellers.restriction.updated. Lift needs a reason; an overturned appeal lifts automatically.

stateMachines.name: Suspension
stateMachines.notes: approve/decline come from access.approval.decided for the named second reviewer. Ending (reinstate, overturned appeal) moves the account through reinstate or reinstateWithRestrictions.

stateMachines.name: Seller warning
stateMachines.notes: Resolve records a note, e.g. 'resolved after 7 days on time'.

stateMachines.name: Seller invitation
stateMachines.notes: apply happens when startApplication uses the invitation code.

stateMachines.name: Appeal
stateMachines.notes: The reviewer can never be the person who made the original decision (SAME_REVIEWER_NOT_ALLOWED). After upheld the seller may file one level-2 appeal, which goes to secondAppealTo. Appeals must be filed before the route's deadline (APPEAL_WINDOW_CLOSED).

stateMachines.name: Change request
stateMachines.notes: Store name, tagline, public claims, legal name, ownership, business address and brand requests. The current value stays live until approval. Ownership changes may also re-run verification checks.

stateMachines.name: Public claim
stateMachines.notes: Only approved claims show on the storefront. Revoke is used when trust finds the claim false; it records a policy violation.

stateMachines.name: Seller member
stateMachines.notes: Accept happens in identity (identity.invitation.accepted). suspend and reactivate are POST /members/{id}/suspend and /reactivate (owner only); revoke cancels the identity invitation (identity.revokeInvitation). The owner cannot be removed or suspended; ownership moves only through an ownership change request.

stateMachines.name: Launch readiness review
stateMachines.notes: Request unlocks when payout readiness is verified and at least one product or offer is submitted. Passing publishes sellers.launch_review.decided; offers then activates the seller's eligible offers (approved product, complete offer with stock).

stateMachines.name: Payout readiness
stateMachines.notes: Mirror of finance's destination review: verified/rejected come from finance.destination.verified / finance.destination.rejected. During a change the old verified destination keeps receiving payouts.

stateMachines.name: Verified seller label
stateMachines.notes: Granted when identity, business registration, payout account and return address checks pass. Lapses verifiedLabelValidDays after it was granted, or earlier when a checked document expires (e.g. business licence renewal). The label always says product authenticity was not checked.

endpoints.summary: Sell with us: requirements, categories, example fees, payout timing, targets, steps
endpoints.desc: Fee examples come from finance fee rules when enabled (finance.calculateFee) and are always marked as examples; agreements from content.currentPolicyVersions.

endpoints.summary: Start a seller application (step 1: seller account)
endpoints.desc: Uses the caller's member account (identity). One open application per account (APPLICATION_EXISTS). During invite-only launch an invitationCode is required unless applicationsOpen. Refused before canReapplyFrom after a rejection.

endpoints.summary: My application with progress, information requests, decision and timeline
Save a step (draft saves at any time)
endpoints.desc: Send one or more step sections. Payout bank numbers are tokenised with the payout provider in this call and never stored; only the label and token are kept. While information is required only the sections named in the request can change.

endpoints.summary: Attach an uploaded document (ID, registration, W-9, bank letter, certificate)
endpoints.desc: Upload the file to media first (PDF, JPG or PNG up to 10 MB), then attach it with its kind.

endpoints.summary: Remove a document from a draft or an open information request
Accept the agreements and submit
endpoints.desc: Records each agreement version with the typed signature, creates the seller row (status applied), starts automated verification checks and sets the decision target. Duplicate checks run in the same call: the tax id hash, payout token, business and return address and work email are matched against other applications and sellers (including closed ones); every match is added to duplicateSignals and sent to trust with trust.raiseSignal (type duplicate_application, subjects the application and the matched seller, dedupeKey per application) when trust is enabled. sellers.application.submitted carries the hashes for trust's own rules. Fails with APPLICATION_INCOMPLETE (details.missing per step) or AGREEMENT_VERSION_OUTDATED if a newer version became effective while the applicant was reading.

acceptances.desc: { key, versionLabel, policyVersionId? } for every required agreement

endpoints.summary: Send the requested information for review
endpoints.desc: Each open item needs a document or an updated section (e.g. a street return address). Moves the application back to under review.

endpoints.summary: Withdraw an application
Appeal a rejection before the deadline
endpoints.desc: A different reviewer decides within appealDecisionDays. Overturning reopens the application under review.

endpoints.summary: Public seller storefront
endpoints.desc: Header, verification explanation, approved claims, highlights, featured collections and category counts in one call. Shipping (shipping), returns (returns), rating (reviews), category counts (search) and promotion (promotions) are read in-process; missing sources go to `unavailable`. Products are listed through search with sellerId; seller feedback through reviews. Closed sellers return 404; suspended sellers return sellingNow=false and no collections.

endpoints.summary: One featured collection with its offer ids
Account status, verification, product approval, payout readiness and active restrictions
endpoints.desc: Three separate indicators as the plan requires. Product approval is aggregated from catalog and offers; payout readiness mirrors finance.

endpoints.summary: Setup checklist and what will go live after the launch review
endpoints.desc: Store profile (sellers), shipping coverage (shipping.hasCoverage), return address (returns), payout verification (finance via payout readiness), first submission (catalog/offers), launch review (sellers).

endpoints.summary: Ask the Seller Manager for the launch readiness review
Legal and contact details
Update contact person, email, phone and support hours
endpoints.desc: No review needed; recorded in the account timeline.

endpoints.summary: Request a change to legal name, ownership or business address
endpoints.desc: Material changes need review and may re-run verification. The seller is told the impact on selling or payouts. Requires reauthToken from POST /api/seller/identity/reauth (single use, checked with identity.verifyReauthToken); a missing, expired or used token returns STEP_UP_REQUIRED.

endpoints.summary: My pending and decided change requests (store name, claims, business)
Withdraw a pending change request
Storefront editor data with pending reviews and live preview data
Save storefront changes
endpoints.desc: Logo, banner, introduction (max introMaxChars), location, contact options and warranty publish on save. A new store name or tagline becomes a change request (kind store_name or tagline) and the current value stays live until approved (decision: the tagline is reviewed like claims). Removing the tagline needs no review.

endpoints.summary: Submit a public claim or brand affiliation with evidence
endpoints.desc: Not shown until staff approve it (claimReviewDays target). Claims without evidence are refused.

endpoints.summary: Ask Marketly to add a brand that is not listed, with evidence
endpoints.desc: Creates a brand_request change request shown in the brand claims waiting list (admin/categories). On approval sellers publishes sellers.change_request.decided (kind brand_request) and catalog adds the brand. A brand needed for one product can still be requested with the product submission in catalog.

endpoints.summary: Withdraw a pending or approved claim
Add a featured collection
endpoints.desc: Only the seller's own offers; offers that are ineligible are kept but hidden from the storefront.

endpoints.summary: Edit a featured collection
Remove a featured collection
Set collection order
Owner and staff with roles, status and last activity
Role templates and the seller permission catalogue (permission matrix)
Invite a staff member
endpoints.desc: Owner only. identity.inviteSellerMember sends a link valid for invitationValidDays. Owner-only and non-delegable permissions are refused (NOT_DELEGABLE).

endpoints.summary: Resend an invitation (new expiry)
Cancel an invitation
Change a member's role or single permissions
endpoints.desc: Takes effect on the member's next request (identity session claims are refreshed). The owner's permissions cannot be changed.

endpoints.summary: Temporarily block a member
Lift a member's suspension
endpoints.desc: suspended → active with the role and permissions the member had. Calls identity.grantSellerContext so the member can act for the seller again on their next request.

endpoints.summary: Remove a member
endpoints.desc: Calls identity.revokeSellerContext so the member's seller sessions end immediately.

endpoints.summary: Account health: metrics vs targets, warnings and actions
Active and past restrictions and suspensions
One restriction: reason, affected activity, what still works, how to resolve, appeal route
Upload documents that resolve a restriction (e.g. brand authorisation)
endpoints.desc: Creates a work item for the Seller Manager to review; it is not an appeal. The item closes when the restriction is lifted or updated (sellers.restriction.lifted, sellers.restriction.updated); a restriction kept unchanged is resolved by hand.

endpoints.summary: Appeal a restriction or suspension before the deadline
endpoints.desc: For a suspension, pass the suspension id in place of a restriction id; both are listed under /restrictions. One open appeal per decision and level.

endpoints.summary: My appeals and their outcomes
Withdraw an appeal
Payout destination label and readiness
Change the payout bank account (owner only)
endpoints.desc: Owner only and never delegable. Requires reauthToken from POST /api/seller/identity/reauth (single use, checked with identity.verifyReauthToken); a missing, expired or used token returns STEP_UP_REQUIRED. Numbers are tokenised with the payout provider; finance then verifies the destination and records a review before any payout goes there. The current verified account keeps receiving payouts meanwhile. The seller is notified of the change and its effect.

endpoints.summary: Accepted agreement versions and new versions waiting for acceptance
Accept a new agreement version (owner)
Owner asks to close the seller account
endpoints.desc: New sales stop at once; the account closes after open orders, returns, cases and the final payout are settled.

endpoints.summary: All sellers with status, verification, rating, on-time dispatch, cases, balance and restrictions
Counts for the sellers header and status tabs
Seller detail: account, restrictions, performance, open obligations, appeals, payouts, notes, history
Add a staff-only note
Set the seller's account manager
Restrict a seller (reason, affected activity, scope, appeal route, review date)
endpoints.desc: Above the caller's authority (access: Recommend only / Permitted with second review) the restriction is saved as pending_approval with an access approval request and the call answers 201 with the Restriction and its approval (ApprovalInfo); it becomes active on access.approval.decided (approved). It never answers APPROVAL_REQUIRED. Active restrictions publish sellers.seller.restricted; offers, promotions and advertising stop only the affected activity. Existing orders, returns, cases and messages keep working.
endpoints.approval: Approval action sellers.sellers.restrict. Second reviewer when the caller's role is 'Permitted with second review' for seller restrictions

endpoints.summary: Edit an active restriction (scope, reason, resolution steps, review date)
endpoints.desc: Audited and republished as sellers.restriction.updated. Above the caller's authority the change is kept in pending_changes with an access approval request and the call answers 200 with the Restriction unchanged, its pendingChange and approval (FORMAT.md, Approval responses); access.approval.decided (approved) applies it, so the caller does not send it again. It never answers APPROVAL_REQUIRED.
endpoints.approval: Approval action sellers.sellers.restrict. Second reviewer when the caller's role is 'Permitted with second review' for seller restrictions

endpoints.summary: Lift a restriction with a reason
What a suspension would do to offers, open orders, returns, cases and payouts
Suspend all new sales (always needs a second reviewer)
endpoints.desc: Creates an access approval request for secondReviewerId and returns 202 with the pending suspension. On access.approval.decided (approved) the status moves to suspended and sellers.seller.suspended is published (offers removed from sale, finance moves balances to Held with the review date, cancel_unshipped_and_refund asks orders to cancel and refund, which itself needs Finance approval). Appeal route: within appealWindowDays, decided by someone else.
endpoints.approval: Approval action sellers.sellers.suspend. Always a second reviewer (Seller Manager or Business Owner)

endpoints.summary: End a suspension (optionally keeping restrictions)
Close a seller account
endpoints.desc: New sales stop; open obligations stay accessible until settled; finance issues the final statement. A closure for another reason than the seller's request always needs a second reviewer: the closure is kept in pending_changes with an access approval request and the call answers 200 with the SellerAccount unchanged, its pendingChange and approval (FORMAT.md, Approval responses); access.approval.decided (approved) applies it, so the caller does not send it again. It never answers APPROVAL_REQUIRED.
endpoints.approval: Approval action sellers.sellers.close. Second reviewer unless the seller requested closure

endpoints.summary: Send a performance or policy warning
Mark a warning resolved
Grant or revoke the Verified seller label
Pass the launch readiness review or ask for changes
Application queue, oldest decision target first
Application with checks, risk flags, documents, notes and timeline
Assign a reviewer
Move a submitted application to Under review
Run an automated check again (e.g. after a new document)
Record a manual check result or accept a 'needs attention' result with a note
Refer the application to Trust and Risk
endpoints.desc: Calls trust.requestAssessment; flags arrive with trust.assessment.completed. Some categories are referred automatically (riskReviewCategories).

endpoints.summary: Ask the applicant for specific items with a deadline
endpoints.desc: Status becomes Information required; the applicant gets an email and a task. The application closes (expired) if there is no reply by the deadline.

endpoints.summary: Approve the application
endpoints.desc: Blocked while checks are failed or need attention without an accepted note (CHECKS_UNRESOLVED). Optional conditions create restrictions at approval (e.g. a category excluded until certificates are checked). Publishes sellers.seller.approved (finance opens the ledger and applies the new-seller hold; returns stores the return address; sellers itself grants the owner seller context with identity.grantSellerContext; identity does not consume this event). Approval does not publish products or enable payouts.

endpoints.summary: Reject with an explanation the applicant will read
Add a staff-only note to an application
Appeals waiting for a decision
Assign an appeal reviewer (not the original decider)
Uphold, overturn or partly overturn
endpoints.desc: Overturn lifts the restriction, ends the suspension or reopens the application. Partly overturn narrows the restriction (changes). The explanation is shown to the seller.

changes.desc: For partly_overturn: new scope, affected activities or review date

endpoints.summary: Store names, taglines, public claims, brand affiliation and business changes waiting for review
Approve or reject a change request or public claim
Remove an approved claim found to be false
Current and scheduled performance targets
Change targets with an effective date
endpoints.desc: Changes state their effective date; metrics already computed are not re-graded. Answers the saved targets. Above the caller's authority the change is kept in pending_changes with an access approval request and the call answers 200 with the current targets (unchanged), the pendingChange and approval (FORMAT.md, Approval responses); access.approval.decided (approved) applies it, so the caller does not send it again. It never answers APPROVAL_REQUIRED.

consumes.name: access.approval.decided
consumes.does: Finish pending suspensions, restrictions, closures and target changes (approved) or cancel them (declined)

consumes.name: trust.assessment.completed
consumes.does: Store risk level, flags and recommendation on the application's risk review

consumes.name: trust.enforcement.recorded
consumes.does: When the action is restrict_seller, warn_seller or suspend_seller, create the restriction or warning from the enforcement parameters (recommendedBy Trust) or start a suspension that still needs its second reviewer; each keeps trustEnforcementId (restrictions, warnings, suspensions) and the resulting event carries it

consumes.name: trust.enforcement.reversed
consumes.does: Undo what the enforcement created (decision D9): restrict_seller lifts the active or pending restriction with that trustEnforcementId (reason from the reversal; sellers.restriction.lifted and, when the status changes, sellers.seller.reinstated); suspend_seller ends the active suspension (reinstate, keeping other restrictions) or cancels one still pending second review; warn_seller resolves the open warning with the reversal note (sellers.warning.resolved). No approval is asked: the reversal was approved in trust. Nothing found (already lifted or never applied) is a no-op; other actions are ignored

consumes.does: Payout readiness → verified; setup checklist step done

consumes.name: finance.destination.rejected
consumes.does: Payout readiness back to not_added (new account) or verified (change rejected, old account stays); tell the owner why

notes: Fulfilled by Marketly: the products_inventory member role template also grants fulfillment-service.inbound.manage and fulfillment-service.fees.view. Members invited with that template before (permissions are stored per member) get the two keys from template_grants (migration 0004): the grant waits while fulfillment-service is off (a key the permission catalogue does not know would make the member uneditable) and is applied once, at the first start where fulfillment-service runs, to every open products_inventory member who lacks it (sellers.member.permissions_changed per member, system actor). Members who later have a key removed keep it removed. Seller performance never counts dispatch facts of groups Marketly fulfils (shipping events with fulfilledBy marketly_service): no on-time, late or overdue fact for the seller.

Principals from actors: access.check and access.requestApproval take an identity.Principal. Endpoints pass the caller's principal; event consumers and jobs that act for a staff member (e.g. trust.enforcement.recorded carrying the Seller Manager who accepted the recommendation) build one from the event's Actor: kind staff, audience admin, accountId = actor.id, sessionId sellers:<actor kind>. Its permissions are what access holds for that account, so authority is checked against the person, never widened.

Payout account changes: every destination handed to finance (the initial one at approval and each owner change) is a payout_changes row (id = changeId in sellers.payout_account.changed): pending until finance.destination.verified (verified: it becomes the current destination and the one it replaces becomes replaced) or finance.destination.rejected (rejected with the reason; payouts keep going to the current destination). At most one row per seller is pending and one is verified (the current destination). Blocked reasons live in sellers.payout_blocked_reasons.

Pending staff changes: a seller closure (sellers.sellers.close), a change to an active restriction and a performance target change that need a second reviewer are kept in pending_changes with the access approval request id; access.approval.decided applies (approved) or drops them. The call answers its normal status with the record unchanged, pendingChange (PendingStaffChange) and approval (ApprovalInfo) in the body (FORMAT.md, Approval responses), never APPROVAL_REQUIRED; the change is applied on approval and is not sent again. Staff views of a seller account (closure) and of a restriction (restriction change) show the pending change until it is decided.

Seller-area endpoints act on the seller in the caller's identity seller context; no seller id appears in seller paths. The kernel guard checks the member's permissions with getMemberAccess on every request.

Seller permissions for other areas (catalog.products.submit, orders, returns, finance view and so on) are declared by their owning modules with audience seller; sellers only assigns them through role templates. sellers.staff.manage, sellers.payout-account.manage, sellers.business.change, sellers.agreements.accept and sellers.account.close are owner-only; payout changes are never delegable (plan ch. 11).

Phase: seller staff invitations and permission edits are phase 2 ('staff access' in plan ch. 20 phase 2); at launch each seller has its owner only. Automatic performance warnings (sellers.auto-warnings) are phase 2 'performance controls'; the metrics, targets, manual warnings, restrictions and appeals are phase 1 because scenario 7 needs them.

Seller support requests from seller/help (CS- references, topics, reply targets) live in support, not here: they share SLAs, assignment and escalation with customer cases. Sellers links the support entry point and passes the restriction or appeal reference as context.

Payout destination: sellers collects and tokenises the details (owner only, step-up) and publishes sellers.payout_account.changed; finance runs micro-deposit verification and the recorded review (finance.destination.verified / rejected) and never pays an unverified destination. The deposit-confirmation screen is finance's (seller/finance).

Return address: collected in the application, then owned by returns. sellers.seller.approved carries it so returns can create the seller's return terms and address (request to the returns owner: consume sellers.seller.approved).

Agreement texts and versions come from content policies (keys seller_agreement, product_rules, fee_schedule, service_standards). If content is off, the versions come from settings and policyVersionId is null.

Restriction events carry everything offers, promotions and advertising need (affected activities and scope) so other sellers' offers and existing orders are untouched (scenario 7). Every restriction end publishes sellers.restriction.lifted (restrictionId); when it also changes the account status, sellers.seller.reinstated follows with liftedRestrictionId or endedSuspensionId and the remaining restriction ids, so offers restores exactly what that restriction or suspension removed and keeps what remaining restrictions still cover. affectedActivities uses one enum everywhere (Restriction, events, canSell).

Trust: application risk checks go through trust.requestAssessment and come back as trust.assessment.completed. When a Seller Manager accepts a 'restrict seller' recommendation in trust, trust records the enforcement and sellers creates the restriction from it (recommendedBy = Trust). Appeals on seller restrictions are always owned here; trust lists linked ones read-only (sellers.appeal.* events).

The admin seller detail aggregates orders (open and overdue orders), returns (open returns), support (open cases) and finance (balances, holds, next payout) in-process; each is optional and reported in `unavailable` when off.

Approval actions (see approvalActions; registered with access): sellers.sellers.restrict (authority; per-role 'Permitted', 'Permitted with second review' or 'Recommend only'), sellers.sellers.suspend (always a second reviewer), sellers.sellers.close (second reviewer unless the seller asked) and sellers.performance.targets (authority).
Applicants use their member account (identity realm member). 'Create a new seller login' in step 1 is an identity registration done by the app before startApplication.

Staff → applicant conversations: messaging calls getApplicationParticipant(applicationId) to add the applicant (identity account, name, work email) as a participant when the conversation starts, so the applicant sees it on sell/status.

Trust reversal (decision D9): restrictions, suspensions and warnings created from a trust enforcement keep trustEnforcementId; trust.enforcement.reversed undoes exactly those records and the resulting sellers.restriction.lifted / sellers.seller.reinstated / sellers.warning.resolved events let offers and the other owners restore what they removed.
